newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada sets second round of specials.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada sets second round of specials.

text.p: The Bank of Canada on Monday conducted a second round of special purchase and resale agreements in the money market at 3.25 percent, traders said.
The central bank intervened after the call loan, or overnight lending rate, continued to be bid at the top of the bank's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.

"There's just some tightness. I guess the U.S. market is part of that. There's dislocations in cash out there and there's a big coupon payment," said one Toronto-based trader. "He (the bank) is just letting the market know that he's there to alleviate this tension."
The call loan rate remained bid at 3.25 percent following the intervention and traders said a third round of specials was possible.
The Bank of Canada set specials this morning after the overnight rate and T-bill yields moved higher amid weakness in U.S. fixed-income markets and Canadian dollar.

Dealers said the weakness in the currency and dislocation in cash markets was partly being prompted by the large number of Government of Canada bonds which pay semiannual coupons at the beginning of December.
The central bank this morning intervened to slow the slide of the dollar, buying Canadian dollars for U.S. dollars at the C$1.3530 level.

The second round of specials was the fifth time in the past three sessions that the Bank of Canada has intervened in the money market at 3.25 percent. The bank set specials twice on Thursday and once on Friday.
